instructions: See docs/ratings.md. Give every season a rating on the absolute scale. Rate the player that season, never their career.

seasons.note: The breakout: two goals in the League Cup final and Liverpool's most dangerous player.
Fifteen assists as a genuinely elite creator; the level that took him to Real Madrid as a starter.
A second Champions League winner's medal but barely a squad player by now; the number bridges the Liverpool peak and the Manchester City decline rather than either.
Four Real Madrid seasons sit in the gap. He came back at 31 visibly slower and without a goal in twenty starts: still a clever footballer, no longer a dangerous one.
Sold to Newcastle in March; the same player at both clubs.
Sold to Newcastle in March; the same player at both clubs.
Eight goals and eight assists in a debut Premier League season at 21; a genuinely good technician in a newly promoted side.
Back from Sampdoria and still one of England's quickest recovery defenders, though past the Italia 90 peak that sits outside this file.
Ever-present at 33 for a relegated side; the pace that defined him had gone.
Nineteen, but already an Ireland international with outstanding technique and twelve goals for a lower-half side; the rating is for what he could do, not for the fee Inter paid.
Three league goals in a season spent largely behind Viduka and Fowler; the ability was unchanged from Coventry, the opportunity was not.
A genuinely fine passer whose career is a list of injuries; rated on the football, which was good rather than elite.
The three seasons missing from the file are three seasons of knee surgery; he came back a slower, purely positional passer.
Eighteen and already unhurried on the ball in a Premier League midfield; rated as the promising teenager, not the Manchester United player.
Nineteen and a first-choice Premier League midfielder; the range of passing was already the best thing about a poor West Ham side.
England-capped and an ever-present, but technically limited enough that the caps are not evidence of ability here.
Thirty-four, twelve starts in a relegated side, and by this point plainly not a top-flight footballer.
Ever-present in the title side and the best defender in it; quick, reads the game, unfussy.
A rotation option at United rather than a first choice, and injured for much of the treble season.
A Champions League semi-final season and comfortable at centre-back in it; the best football of his career.
His best season, and a British record fee for a defender followed. The fee is not the reason for the number.
The best stretch of his career: five England caps followed at 31, at an age when most full-backs are declining.
Thirty-three and reduced to eleven starts as Charlton looked past him.
Ever-present and his best season; a shade above the 84 anchor rather than a different player.
Back trouble and a Middlesbrough side that asked far more of him at 33.
Eight starts and retirement at 35, with the back trouble that ended him.
Twenty at the start of the Double season and first choice for it; the athleticism and the recovery pace were already exceptional, the defensive detail still coming.
The best left-back in the league at 22 and England’s first choice.
The season of his public confession and rehabilitation; he was some way short of himself on the pitch.
Restored, and arguably the best season of his career: ever-present, Arsenal's creative hub, and back in the England squad for Euro 96.
The Division One year at Middlesbrough is not in the file; he returned at close to his Arsenal level, briefly.
The Division One year at Middlesbrough is not in the file; he returned at close to his Arsenal level, briefly.
Thirty-five starts as the screen in front of the defence in the Everton side that finished fourth; the best season of his career, at 30.
Seventeen goals and nine assists in his second English season; the centre-forward’s instincts had arrived and the pace was already unplayable.
Twenty-four league goals in the Double season; by now among the best forwards in the world.
Twenty-four goals and twenty assists, PFA and FWA Player of the Year. Statistically the most complete attacking season of the era and a point short of the 2003/04 anchor.

Anchor season (97). The jump from 85 in his first English campaign reflects four years of development: in 1999/00 he was a converted winger still learning the centre-forward role, not the finished article.
Twenty-five goals and fourteen assists in thirty-one starts; still at the level of the anchor season, with a little less of the year-long invincibility.
Thirty-one and a wide forward in a side built around Messi: still a serious player, no longer the one the whole thing runs through.
Below his 1997/98 self on the ball, but already an elite organiser and defender.
Thirty-four, ten starts and a final season; still the organiser, no longer able to play every week.
Same rating at Charlton and on the Tottenham loan; one player, one season.
Same rating at Charlton and on the Tottenham loan; one player, one season.
Thirty-seven starts, seven goals and nine assists in a Newcastle side that finished fourth; the best crosser and dead-ball striker in the division that season.
Sold to Aston Villa in January; the same player at both clubs.
Sold to Aston Villa in January; the same player at both clubs.
Twenty-three in his first English season and immediately Chelsea’s quickest and most athletic defender; capable at centre-back and either full-back without loss.
Mostly at left-back in a title-winning side that conceded fifteen; elite as a defender, and better still for being able to do it anywhere across the back four.
PFA and FWA Player of the Year in a double season. First touch and vision of an all-time great forward; held below 95 by the absence of pace and the modest goal volume.
Nineteen starts and three goals - his leanest Arsenal return. The touch and the passing are untouched; the numbers are not the judgement.
Thirty-four and rotated through the Invincibles season; still the best technician in the side.
Four starts through injury; rated as the player, not on the appearances.
Joined Newcastle in February 1996.
Joined Newcastle in February 1996.
Returned to Leeds in December 1998.
Returned to Leeds in December 1998.
Achilles and rib injuries had reduced him to ten starts by 34, and the legs the Enforcer game depended on were gone.
The best defender in a Forest side that finished ninth, and comfortable enough on the ball to be unusual for a 1990s centre-half.
Ever-present in Bradford's survival season, which is evidence about a hard-working side rather than a step up in ability.
PFA Young Player of the Year at 19; six goals and nine assists from the left.
Ten league goals for a side that finished third; one of the best wide players in the division at 20.
Twelve starts — injury rather than a fall in level.
Fourteen league goals from the left in a poor Leeds side; the peak version of him.
Thirty-six starts at Liverpool but shunted between roles and rarely decisive; a genuine drop, not just a change of club.
Chronic groin trouble reduced him to fifteen starts; he was never the same athlete afterwards.
Took the Wimbledon shirt for good and became Scotland's first choice; a very good shot-stopper for a modest side.
Four starts as Cudicini’s deputy at Chelsea; rated as the keeper, not the appearances.
Twenty-one and in his first English season; quick and composed, but not yet the player of his mid-twenties.
Settled as United’s left-sided defender and a France international; quick and strong, always prone to a lapse.
Twenty-three goals and the Golden Boot in his first Chelsea season; a powerful, ferocious finisher, kept just below the van Nistelrooy anchor (90) on all-round play.
Thirty-two and at Middlesbrough; still an ever-present with thirteen goals, but the explosiveness had gone.
Two seasons on from the teenager of 1998/99 and three years older; the dribbling had become a genuine Premier League weapon.
Nineteen, thirty-four starts and eight league goals in a survival season; the timing of the runs into the box was the finished part of his game from the start.
Twenty-three league goals and an England call-up; powerful and a genuinely good finisher, but a narrow forward, so held well below the Phillips 1999/00 mark.
Split between Southampton and Everton after a January move; four goals in eighteen starts across the two and struggling for rhythm at both.
Split between Southampton and Everton after a January move; four goals in eighteen starts across the two and struggling for rhythm at both.
Still a utility player filling in across the back and midfield in his first season; the athleticism was obvious, the centre-back was not yet.
A converted midfielder who was an unbeaten side’s first-choice centre-back at 22; pace and recovery already elite.
Breakthrough at 20: 25 goals and 11 assists as a first-choice forward after a raw, in-and-out first season.
Nine starts: hernia and knee trouble wrecked the season.
Three goals in a relegation season. The output collapsed; on the evidence of 1997/98 and of Celtic afterwards, the player did not collapse with it.
One league goal at Chelsea, often played wide and out of position. Rated as the forward he still was, not as the season looked.
Six years at Celtic in between; back in England at thirty-two he is a bench forward with the touch intact and nothing else.
The blocking, front-foot half of the treble season’s centre-back pair; no distribution to speak of, but as good a pure defender as there was in the division that year.
Fifteen starts; injuries and the arrival of younger legs.
Rated as the 20-year-old breaking through after two broken legs, not the England player he became.
The rise from the 1992/93 rating spans two seasons lost to broken legs; he came back a materially better player and was an ever-present for a side that finished third.
Five starts before a knee injury he never properly recovered from; the pace never came back.
The screening midfielder of the treble side; positionally outstanding and a far better passer than the role suggested.
Ever-present at 23 and, on reading of the game and recovery pace, close to the best defender in the division; the knee that later limited him had not yet done so.
Four starts: the knee has taken his season, not his ability. Rated as the defender he still was on the days he could play.
A first Premier League season at 23 and immediately Villa’s best defender; strong, quick across the ground, entirely without frills.
